## Network reachability (anonymous probe)

Anonymous `GET {PROD_URL}/wp-json` — no credentials. Answers only "can this environment
reach the host?" On Desktop this is the egress gate that must pass before any
Application Password is requested.

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Probe URL | {PROD_URL}/wp-json |
| HTTP status | {ANON_PROBE_STATUS} |
| Round-trip | {ANON_PROBE_TIME} |
| Result | {ANON_PROBE_RESULT} |

## Authenticated identity

Authenticated `GET /wp/v2/users/me?_fields=id,name,roles` — confirms the credential
works and records who we are connected as (this drives the operate-phase capability
checks in `04-rest-capabilities.md`).

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Production URL | {PROD_URL} |
| Connected user (login) | {WP_USER} |
| Display name | {WP_DISPLAY_NAME} |
| User ID | {WP_USER_ID} |
| Roles | {ROLES} |
| Auth check | {AUTH_RESULT} |

## What REST cannot see here

- **The Application Password value.** Never read from REST, never stored in this folder
  in clear except the floor `credential` file (when `Tier: portable-file`).
- **Server / proxy details** of the path between here and WordPress — only the final
  HTTP status, not where a `000`/`403` originated (egress proxy vs WordPress). The
  `env` field above is what disambiguates a Desktop egress-403 from a WP-capability-403.
- **Other Application Passwords** on this user, or the AP's own metadata (created date,
  last-used IP). Manage those in `{PROD_URL}/wp-admin/profile.php`.
